transcript.text: dryer drum wont turn but i can here it running, hotpiont. clothes just sit there

Stop using it and unplug it before checking anything. A dryer running with the drum stationary can overheat clothes and potentially damage the heater/motor.

If you can hear the motor/fan running but the drum does not rotate, the most likely cause is:

• Broken or slipped drive belt — very common. The motor runs but no longer drives the drum.
• Less commonly: jammed drum/rollers, a failed tension pulley, or a motor issue.

Quick safe check:

1. Unplug the dryer and remove the laundry.
2. Try turning the drum by hand.
• Turns unusually easily / freely: likely a snapped or detached belt.
• Very stiff, scraping, or won’t turn: something may be jammed or the drum bearings/rollers may have failed.
• Turns normally by hand but not under power: belt/tensioner is still the main suspect.

A belt/tensioner repair normally requires removing panels, so if you are not used to appliance repairs, book a dryer engineer. Have the full Hotpoint model number from the door opening or rear label ready.

Don’t keep running it “just to dry a little” — the clothes won’t tumble and the dryer may overheat.
ok unplugged it and the drum spins really easy by hand almost no resistance. model sticker is worn but it starts TVHM8

That strongly points to a snapped or slipped drum drive belt. If the motor is audibly running and the empty drum spins with almost no resistance, it is no longer being driven by the motor.

“TVHM8…” is likely a Hotpoint 8 kg tumble-dryer range (often TVHM80 variants). The final letters/numbers matter for ordering parts, so try to find the complete model/service number:

• Around the door opening/door frame
• Rear panel label
• Inside the condenser-flap area, if it is a condenser model
• Sometimes printed on the original manual or retailer receipt

The repair is usually: replace/refit the belt and inspect the tensioner pulley. A belt can come off because the tensioner pulley has seized or failed, so it is worth checking rather than only fitting a new belt.

Common symptoms matching yours:
• Dryer sounds normal
• Heater/fan may still work
• Drum does not rotate
• Drum turns extremely freely by hand

Do not run it again until repaired. A non-turning heated drum can overheat the load and the machine.

If you want to repair it yourself, search for a guide using the full model number plus “drum belt replacement.” Before buying, match the belt part number to your exact model rather than relying on “TVHM8” alone.
